title: King Bihkard and the Captured Rebel
summary: Bakhtiyar related the story of King Bihkard of ancient Persia:
full_text:
Bakhtiyar related the story of King Bihkard of ancient Persia:

'King Bihkard defeated a formidable rebel chieftain named Ardashir, who had led an insurrection in the northern mountains for ten years. Captured in the final battle, Ardashir was brought into the royal palace in chains, bruised, defiant, and expecting the scaffold.

The king’s viziers shouted unanimously: "Off with his head! Strike him down, sire, as a warning to all rebels!"

King Bihkard looked upon the captive chieftain, stepped down from his golden throne, and with his own hands struck the iron chains from Ardashir’s wrists!

The king said with noble serenity: "Ardashir, you are a valiant warrior of ancient blood. We fought for ten years because we misunderstood each other’s hearts. Today, victory is mine; and my victory is to grant you life, honor, and complete pardon. Return to your mountains in peace, or remain as my brother."

Ardashir stood dumbfounded, tears streaming down his scarred cheeks. He fell at the king’s feet, kissed his sandals, and wept:

"O King! For ten years I hated your crown, but today your clemency has conquered my soul! By the heavens, the blade that sought your throne shall henceforth be your truest shield."

Ardashir became King Bihkard’s most faithful general, defending the frontiers of the empire against all invaders for thirty years, proving that mercy builds fortresses that no army can overthrow.'
moral: Magnanimous clemency transforms a mortal enemy into the most faithful defender of the realm.
